 3. Tuka Mia died leaving behind 3 sons Kobbat Mia, Abdul Gafur and-Kala Mia and one daughter Badrun Nesa. The heirs of Tuka Mia jointly sold 1.18 acres of land by a registered kabala dated 18.1.1968 to Azizul Hoq. While Azizul Hoq was in possession of the said land sold the same to the late plaintiff Md. Belayet Hossain by a registered kabala dated 19.4.1969. Out of the said 1.18 acres of land .88 acres of land has been correctly recovered in the name of Kobbat Mia and others in Plot No.531 at Ayubpur mouja but the remaining .38 acres of land has been wrongly recorded in plot No.40 in Khatian No.1 in the name of the Government but there was no reason for such recording. The plaintiff had no knowledge about the said wrong record of right but on 02.8.1988 the plaintiff came to know about the said wrong record of right, hence the suit. 

 7. The defendant No.1 against the said judgment of the trial Court preferred Title Appeal No.17 of 1992 in the Court of District Judge, Noakhali which has been ultimately heard by the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Noakhali. During the pendency of the appeal in the appellate Court below one Mozibul Hoq son of Soleman was added as respondent No.2 in the appeal who filing a written statement in the appellate Court below averred that Tuka Mia while was -exercising his right, title and possession into 2.70 acres of land, the land was sold in auction and Sree Prosanna Kumar Das had purchased the land and the said sale was confirmed on 15.11.1924 and in the M.R. record of right the land was correctly recorded in his name in Khatian No.6 and 9. In the Diara settlement 2.24 acres of land out of the said 2.70 acres of land was wrongly recorded in the name of Kobbat Mia and others, the heirs of Tuka Mia. The remaining .46 acres of land was wrongly recorded in Plot No.40 in Khatian No.1 in the name of the government. 

 11. On the other hand, Mr. Md. Osman.Gani Khan, the learned Assistant Attorney General appearing for the defendant-opposite party No.1 opposes the Rule. He submits that the suit land has been recorded in Plot No.40 in Khatian No.1 in the name of the Government. Both the plaintiff of the present suit and the added respondent No.2 Mozibul Hoq of the appeal have been claiming the suit land and apart from the present suit there appears another suit pending in the Court below filed by Mozibul Hoq for the same land. So, for proper adjudication and also for an effective and complete justice both the suits should be heard analogously by the trial Court. He also submits that the appellate Court below in order to render equal justice to all the parties had sent the suit back on remand which does not call for any interference from this Court. 

 13. On going to the materials on record it appears that initially the plaintiff had come in the trial Court with a very simple case that he purchased the suit land from Azizul Hoq and Azizul Hoq got the suit land from the heirs of recorded tenant Tuka Mia but in the Diara settlement .38 acres of land has been wrongly recorded in the name of the Government in Plot No.40 in Khatian No.1. 

 15. Mozibul Hoq though admitted that the suit land originally belonged to Tuka Mia but his further case is that the land has been sold in an auction and one Prosanna Kumar Das purchased the suit land in the said auction and pursuant to the said purchase in auction the M.R. Khatian was also prepared in the name of Prosanna Kumar Das but in the Diara settlement 2.24 acres of land has been wrongly recorded in the name of the heirs of Tuka Mia and remaining .46 acres of land has been wrongly recorded in the name of the Government and Mozibul Hoq filed a suit for declaration of his title into the said land which is still pending in the competent Court for disposal.
